title: Cast Iron vs. PVC in Acoustic Drainage Performance
description: Material selection plays a critical role in drainage system design, particularly regarding noise attenuation and fire resistance. Cast iron piping possesses high density and structural mass, which significantly dampens fluid velocity noise as wastewater travels down vertical stacks through living spaces. In contrast, lightweight Schedule 40 PVC pipe is economical and chemically resistant, but readily transfers fluid noise through wall cavities unless surrounded by specialized acoustic insulation. Understanding these core material properties allows installers and designers to select the right piping material based on acoustic expectations, building structure, and application requirements.
